Unitary Fourier diagonalization gives the exact longest-cycle norm, including the zero case L=2, α=1/2. Matrix-log expansion proves both nα and n(1−α) boundary limits. Poisson semigroup invertibility and Fourier decay prove sharpness. Standalone verify.py passed direct nonlinear, critical-window and spectral checks; the analytical proof covers all dimensions and times.

value.rationale: At a known qualitative transition from periodic to convergent population states, the theorem determines two different relaxation clocks and two sharp singular boundary profiles, including a residue-sensitive one. These laws quantify finite-time persistence of cyclic populations and identify the longest-cycle rate, a motivated dynamical invariant absent from the primary omega-limit classification. It makes no novelty claim for generic Markov-chain diagonalization or the matrix exponential.
